scope: Unreleased Scene2D v2: independent flat instances of shared OC/projection definitions across source, editor, layout history, transactions, export, Godot builds and runtime events.
implementation: Author v2 actors carry a unique scene-local instanceId and may repeat definition objectId. New scenes default to v2; old v1 upgrades only through an explicit checked save. Clone/add mint UUIDs; upgrade seeds old definition UUIDs; definition changes, inheritance switches and reorder preserve instance IDs.

JSON source model, build plan and preview envelope support versions1/2. Snapshot envelope stays version1 with a versioned plan. Provenance carries both identities outside frozen snapshots; duplicate/invalid IDs and >128 actors reject. v2 recovery stays strict for duplicate JSON keys and source budgets; v1 legacy recovery behavior stays compatible.

Lossless actor matching follows instance IDs. Upgrade/reorder/save preserve untouched author fragments, BOM, CRLF and numeric spelling; scene.update refuses identity-losing v2-to-v1 downgrade. Existing two-file transaction journals are reused with explicit source and registration recovery tests.

Preview, hit testing, field navigation, layout selection, move and history use sceneActorIdentity. Rust geometry and draft protocol remain unchanged: only the JS adapter maps instanceId to the protocol opaque key named objectId; author definition IDs are preserved.

Definition relations and shared images are deduplicated. A selected resource-package roundtrip retains both instances, their shared definition, owned story and image. Capture/resource-error provenance resolves the affected instance rather than the first repeated definition.

Version-dispatched Godot generation preserves legacy generator/runtime bytes and fingerprint. v2 source maps, nodes and runtime frames carry paired instance and definition IDs; spoofed/mismatched/downgraded frames reject. Import diagnostics are bounded before per-instance expansion: at most256 records,4096 message characters each.

steps: Existing v1 opens without conversion. Explicit upgrade seeds stable IDs, Duplicate creates a new ID for the same definition, and reorder retains all IDs. Preview is read-only; Save preserves BOM/CRLF and changes only the scene source.
English/Japanese language switches retain the checked instance IDs and draft; the Japanese form fits a real 390px viewport.
A real canvas click selects the cloned instance, and its position source link focuses the actual editor and selects /actors/0/position after reorder, with BOM/CRLF preserved on disk.

Real pointer dragging, Undo/Redo, coordinate edits and save operate on the selected instance only. The other instance of the same definition remains at [160,200]; reopening preserves both independent positions and IDs.
An external revision between Check and Apply refuses the stale save without overwriting disk, and keeps the selected instance draft for recovery. The entire UI workflow never launches a build job.
No Godot is configured: the Preview tab renders both frozen SVG images at inherited/overridden sizes and center positions, with source-aware resolved projection fields. No build job runs.
Real pointer selection opens the correct actor inspector. Zoom, grid, pointer pan and Fit visibly affect only the camera and overlay.
A second layout multiplies the inherited image by its RGBA tint and draws the later actor on top; a real center click selects that top actor.
Explicit imageResourceId:null removes inherited imagery. Arrow-key tab navigation maintains ARIA/focus, while English/Japanese and a 390px viewport retain the same scene without horizontal overflow.
A delayed old-scene response cannot replace a newer scene or restore its old images after rapid selection.
Invalid scene dimensions clear old pixels and show a source-located diagnostic. All previews, tab switches and gestures leave authoring files byte-identical and never create a build job.
Edit scene opens from the preview. Saving updates the title and actor position in a fresh preview while preserving scene UUID, BOM/CRLF and every other authored file.
Actor and original-OC source links return to the corresponding document; reopening Preview retains the selected scene and reads a fresh snapshot. Navigation is read-only.

Field links select the exact JSON value in the actual source textarea: the saved scene position survives BOM, CRLF, Chinese and emoji offset conversion, and inherited speed selects the projection configuration. Composite size opens its document without selecting an approximate range.
Changing the scene on disk after preview capture opens the current source and reports a stale location with no selection or write. Restoring the test fixture restores every author-file hash.
SVG images render as image content: embedded script and external-image URLs never execute or request network access.

packagedResources.scope: Offline preparation and actual packaged model/plan/layout WASM/runtime module execution; not native GUI or device acceptance.

nativeCore.scope: Built unchanged native CLI offline to enable parity, no new Rust semantic migration.

iterations: Read-only review reproduced shared-resource error amplification:100 log lines with128 instances emitted12801 diagnostics. v2 now bounds count and line length before expanding; regression tests cover repeated and oversized lines.

Initial preview fixture incorrectly used explicit null with a non-inherited actor, which existing semantics reject. Corrected fixture omits the image field for that actor; final14 preview tests pass. Initial normal-isolation wrapper hid child details, so targeted no-isolation run revealed the fixture assertion.

First complete run passed1232 with19skips and one old projection UI assertion expecting default v1. Updated it to assert defaultv2 and stable instance ID across definition and inheritance switches; final full run passes.
limitations: Nineteen native archive/mobile helper cases skipped because those helpers were not supplied. Shared core parity and actual Godot4.7.2 enabled. Selected resource-package Node roundtrip is covered; no new full native archive/device acceptance claimed.
Scene hierarchy, reusable fragments, screenplay events, arbitrary author scripts and >128-actor scalability remain planned. Instance semantics remain portable JS; Rust core receives opaque keys.
Old clients are not claimed universally read-only: format-aware operations retain version gates, while old generic source editors can still edit author text.
No Tauri/Android window or device acceptance, installer, version bump, commit, push or installation.
cleanup: All checks use disposable fixtures. Offline prepared resources and cache copies removed; staging/native build target removed after guarded synchronization. Existing author workspaces/configuration and prior evidence not changed.
